value.description: The ID exactly as the outside source writes it, before rkey cleanup, e.g. 'NFL.10~17:2026-11-08'.

league.description: League code, when the outside ID is only unique within a league.

scheme.description: Whose ID this is. 'slug' is a readable slug from this convention; 'old' is a retired slug of ours.

target.description: The canonical record this resolves to.

alternates.description: Other records the same value could mean, e.g. a shared nickname. 'target' is the default pick (the higher-level, more common team).

main.description: Record key is '<scheme>:<kind>:<value>', all lowercase, with every character outside a-z 0-9 . - _ ~ : replaced by '-'. For IDs that repeat across leagues (ESPN team IDs), the league code goes before the value, e.g. 'espn:team:nfl:4' (league 'nfl', value '4'). Other examples: 'espn:league:eng.1', 'slug:team:bearcats', 'sideline:team:nfl-chargers', 'slug:game:nfl-2026-11-09-cin-pit', 'old:team:nfl-oak', '2ndscreen:team:nfl:4' (value is 2nd Screen's own record key 'nfl:4', which already includes the league).

description: One entry in the shared slug map: an outside ID, an old slug or a readable slug, pointing at the canonical league, team, person, game or event record. Lets anyone resolve an ID with a single getRecord call, no index needed.
